id: cuad:VAPOTHERM, INC. - Manufacturing and Supply Agreement

findings.quoted_text: Medica shall use [* * *] efforts to develop technical know-how that would permit them to manufacture the Cartridge less expensively and shall no less than semiannually furnish the Joint Review Committee with a detailed report as to their progress in this area.

by Vapotherm, if for any reason other than an Event of Force Majeure Medica fails to deliver within [* * *] days after the required delivery date, or on more than two occasions in any [* * *]-day period fails to deliver within [* * *] days after the required delivery day, any shipment of Cartridge it is required to deliver pursuant to Section 3.2, Section 4.2, or Section 9.3;
Vapotherm shall pay each such invoice in full within [* * *] Calendar Days from the date of invoice, unless Vapotherm has rejected the shipment in question in accordance with Section 4.2.
This limitation does not, however, apply to any obligation of either party to indemnify the other in connection with any Indemnifiable Loss.

Medica shall use [* * *] efforts to develop technical know-how that would permit them to manufacture the Cartridge less expensively and shall no less than semiannually furnish the Joint Review Committee with a detailed report as to their progress in this area.
findings.explanation: This clause forces Medica to invest resources into ongoing cost-reduction R&D and provide detailed reports without guaranteeing additional compensation or reimbursement.
findings.suggested_change: Clarify that cost-reduction research is voluntary or that any resulting R&D efforts will be compensated under a separate, mutually agreed statement of work.

findings.quoted_text: by Vapotherm, if for any reason other than an Event of Force Majeure Medica fails to deliver within [* * *] days after the required delivery date, or on more than two occasions in any [* * *]-day period fails to deliver within [* * *] days after the required delivery day, any shipment of Cartridge it is required to deliver pursuant to Section 3.2, Section 4.2, or Section 9.3;
findings.explanation: Vapotherm can terminate the agreement immediately based on delivery delays occurring multiple times, putting Medica at severe risk of contract cancellation without proportional protections for supply chain disruptions.
findings.suggested_change: Include a broader cure mechanism or extend the allowable window for minor delays before triggering a termination right.

findings.quoted_text: Vapotherm shall pay each such invoice in full within [* * *] Calendar Days from the date of invoice, unless Vapotherm has rejected the shipment in question in accordance with Section 4.2.
findings.explanation: Depending on the length of the payment window, extended payment terms combined with rejection withholding rights can create cash flow strain for Medica.
findings.suggested_change: Specify a reasonable, short payment window and restrict withholding to only the specific disputed portion of rejected goods.

findings.quoted_text: This limitation does not, however, apply to any obligation of either party to indemnify the other in connection with any Indemnifiable Loss.
findings.explanation: This carve-out from the damage limitations exposes Medica to potentially open-ended exposure for third-party indemnification claims.
findings.suggested_change: Ensure that all indemnification obligations are explicitly subject to the overall liability cap.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello, I hope you are doing well. I am writing to suggest a few minor revisions to the agreement prior to signing. - Regarding the provision on cost-reduction research, it requires ongoing work without guaranteed compensation, so I propose clarifying that such research is voluntary or separately compensated. - Regarding the termination terms for delivery delays, the current text allows immediate cancellation for minor issues, so I propose including a broader cure mechanism or extending the allowable window. - Regarding the payment clause, the current terms may cause cash flow strain, so I propose specifying a reasonable payment window and restricting withholding to disputed portions. - Regarding the liability carve-out, the current wording creates open-ended exposure for third-party claims, so I propose ensuring all indemnification obligations are subject to the overall liability cap. Thank you for your time, and I look forward to finalizing the agreement.
